claim: A review of 25 studies using the stimulated-vs-baseline design found 14 manipulated variables (about the inspiration source and the design process) and wide differences in methods and results; the authors call for more consistent methods.
title: Inspiration and fixation: Questions, methods, findings, and challenges
transfer: Warns that fixation effects vary by setup. Test anti-fixation steps on our own tasks; do not assume a fixed effect size.

claim: In an experiment with 97 domain experts, two design-by-analogy methods (WordTree, SCAMPER) raised idea novelty versus control; WordTree reduced fixation, SCAMPER did not, though it gave more novel ideas.
authors: Moreno, D. P.; Blessing, L. T.; Yang, M. C.; Hernandez, A. A.; Wood, K. L.
title: Overcoming design fixation: Design by analogy studies and nonintuitive findings
transfer: Novelty prompts and fixation reduction are separate things. Measure both: distinct answers and copy-of-example rate.

claim: Controlled test with 280 participants: LLM help (free-form, direct generation, theory-structured) did not improve problem-frame quality, widened the gap between experienced and inexperienced designers, and lowered novices' sense of agency.
quote: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
authors: Shin, J.; Polyanskaya, A.; Lucero, A.; Oulasvirta, A.
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
transfer: Do not assume an LLM reframe step helps. Gate any frame step by an equal-token test against plain. Humans used the LLM here; an agent loop with a check is untested.

claim: LLM design agents can fixate on existing paradigms; a self-regulation loop and a separate co-regulation agent both beat a plain loop on one battery-pack design test without much added compute, and co-regulation was best.
quote: these systems are prone to some of the same pathologies that plague humans
authors: Xu, Z.; Martelaro, N.; McComb, C.
title: Supervising Ralph Wiggum: Exploring a Metacognitive Co-Regulation Agentic AI Loop for Engineering Design
transfer: A separate monitor call asking 'is the agent stuck on one paradigm?' on open-ended routes only. Single task, preprint: replicate.

claim: Dorst and Cross analysed protocols of nine experienced industrial designers on one task; creative moments came with a bridge that fits a refined problem frame and a partial solution together (problem-solution co-evolution).
title: Creativity in the design process: co-evolution of problem-solution
transfer: Bridge step on open routes: restate the problem so two partial ideas both fit, then generate once more, capped at 2 cycles. Publisher page would not open; n from the earlier brief and memory.

claim: Kruger and Cross found four strategies among nine designers (problem-driven, solution-driven, information-driven, knowledge-driven) and no simple link between strategy and solution quality.
title: Solution driven versus problem driven design: strategies and outcomes
transfer: Do not hard-code 'analyse the problem first'. Page returned 403 here; claim from the earlier brief, which said it checked the abstract.

claim: Jansson and Smith showed designers exposed to an example with flaws reproduced those flaws more than controls (design fixation); this is the founding study of the field.
authors: Jansson, D. G.; Smith, S. M.
title: Design fixation
transfer: Show lessons or examples after first generation, not before, on open tasks. Effect size not verified.

claim: Sio, Kotovsky and Cagan reviewed the role of examples in design: examples can both fixate and inspire. I could not open the paper; search returned only a reference-list entry, so the 'meta-analytic' label and the findings are from memory.
quote: Fixation or inspiration? A meta-analytic review of the role of examples on design processes
authors: Sio, U. N.; Kotovsky, K.; Cagan, J.
title: Fixation or inspiration? A meta-analytic review of the role of examples on design processes
transfer: Examples help or hurt by timing and type; test lesson-before vs lesson-after. Get the pooled effect before relying on it.

claim: Schon's reflection-in-action and on-action are an essay-level framework (book); I know of no controlled test of them as procedures.
title: The Reflective Practitioner
transfer: Inspiration only: let real check output (back talk) trigger reframing, not a timer.

claim: Adams, Turns and Atman coded engineering students' protocols with Schon's theory; seniors showed more problem setting and attention to back talk than freshmen (per the earlier brief; effect sizes not checked).
authors: Adams, R. S.; Turns, J.; Atman, C. J.
title: Educating effective engineering designers: the role of reflective practice
transfer: Measured reflective behaviours could code our agent traces: does the agent react to failing outputs?

claim: Atman et al. compared engineering students and expert practitioners on a design task; experts spent more time scoping the problem and gathered more information (from memory, not re-verified).
authors: Atman, C. J.; Adams, R. S.; Cardella, M. E.; Turns, J.; Mosborg, S.; Saleem, J.
title: Engineering design processes: a comparison of students and expert practitioners
transfer: Protocol-code agent traces into scope / gather / solve moves to see if the agent rushes like a novice. Rushing is often right on single-answer tasks.

claim: Cross's overview of design expertise says expert designers frame the problem and steer search rather than analysing everything first; novices are more solution-fixed (summary from memory).
title: Expertise in design: an overview
transfer: Supports a frame step on ill-defined problems only.

claim: Darke's interview study of architects described a primary generator: an early simple guiding idea tested against the problem and revised; Lawson reports it.
title: The primary generator and the design process
transfer: Matches 'conjecture first, then test': name one guiding idea, state what it predicts, reframe only if the check fails.

claim: The Vasconcelos and Crilly review reports that its 25 studies differ widely in methods and results. No pooled effect size for design fixation appeared in anything I could open, so none is established here.
quote: differ widely in methods and results
title: Inspiration and fixation: Questions, methods, findings, and challenges
transfer: Do not quote effect sizes for fixation in the design doc. Run our own test.

claim: Gap: I found no controlled test that a Dorst-Cross style co-evolution procedure, run inside an LLM at equal tokens, beats plain generation. The search budget ran out before I could look for later work, so this means not found, not that none exists.
title: negative result of a limited search
transfer: Our own equal-token arm (with vs without bridge step) would be a first test.
